intelligence.human_view: A checker's citation became a law that never existed. The checker report quoted "Intelligent Block Rules LAW §4.11/C9 — NO voice anywhere on the board," the captain repeated it to him as a law, and the feed round's Play verdict (NOT PASS) was decided on that basis. He corrected it: his decision was never a ban — it was practical. The voice couldn't play instantly on the boards, it would take up a lot of resources, there would be a delay, and the boards are already beautiful and easy to read. So no voice on the boards for now — not because it is banned, but because it didn't make sense that way. And he DOES want Naya playback everywhere, of course — mostly pre-recorded Naya right now, on the pages and cards that don't change, the whole walkthrough, every slide, possibly the visual collective chain technology, as many places as possible — all at the end, once everything is done complete, so voice is never recorded twice. The open question is the instant one: where playback makes sense and where it does not, and how playback is instant when they click — pre-recorded audio, made beforehand and served from the edge, is the path; a live board whose words change cannot be pre-recorded, and that part is unsolved. This is a correction compound in the full sense: the lesson (SN-3115) + the law-book correction (the §4.11/C9 wording, his hand) + the brief-template update (no brief may cite a voice ban as law) + PI + GitHub. A checker's citation of a rule is not the rule — his word is the rule.
intelligence.simple_view: There's no rule that says "no voice allowed"! The voice just couldn't play fast enough on the boards — it had to think first, and that made people wait. So for now, no voice on the boards. But Naya WILL talk to you — her voice is already recorded on the pages, like a little wave you can play, and she'll tell you all about that page! And every slide of the walkthrough will have her voice too!
